questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From the top of a cliff 50 m high, the angles of depression of the top and bottom of a tower are observed to be $30^{\circ}$ and $45^{\circ}$. The height of tower is
questions.solution: Accoding to condition, Let, height of tower $=h$ In $\triangle A B D, \quad \tan 45^{\circ}=\frac{A B}{B D} \Rightarrow B D=50 \mathrm{~m}$ Now, In $\triangle A C C^{\prime}\begin{aligned} & & \tan 30^{\circ} & =\frac{A C^{\prime}}{C^{\prime} C} \\ \Rightarrow & & \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & =\frac{50-h}{50} \\ \Rightarrow & & 50 & =50 \sqrt{3}-h \sqrt{3} \\ \Rightarrow & & h \sqrt{3} & =50(\sqrt{3}-1) \\ & & h & =50\left(1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) \\ & & & =50\left(1-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\right) \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $A B C$ is a triangular park with $A B=A C=100 \mathrm{~m}$. A TV tower stands at the mid-point of $B C$. The angles of elevation of the top of the tower at $A$, $B, C$ are $45^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}$ respectively. The height of the tower is
questions.solution: According to question, Let $D E=h$ and $C D=D B=x$ In $\triangle E B D, \quad \tan 60^{\circ}=\frac{h}{x} \Rightarrow x=\frac{h}{\sqrt{3}}$ Now, in $\triangle A D E\begin{aligned} & \tan 45^{\circ}=\frac{E D}{D A} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad D A=h \end{aligned}$ In $\triangle A B D$, by applying Pythagoras theorem $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad\left(\frac{h}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^2+h^2=100^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{4 h^2}{3}=10000 \quad \Rightarrow h=50 \sqrt{3} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\alpha$ be the solution of $16^{\sin ^2 \theta}+16^{\cos ^2 \theta}=10$ in $\left(0, \frac{\pi}{4}\right)$. If the shadow of a vertical pole is $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ of its height, then the altitude of the sun is
questions.solution:
We have, $16^{\sin ^2 \theta}+16^{\cos ^2 \theta}=10\Rightarrow \quad 16^{\sin ^2 \theta}+16^{1-\sin ^2 \theta}=10\Rightarrow x+\frac{16}{x}=10$, where $x=16^{\sin ^2 \theta}\Rightarrow \quad x^2-10 x+16=0 \Rightarrow x=2,8\therefore \quad 16^{\sin ^2 \theta}=2,8 \Rightarrow 2^{4 \sin ^2 \theta}=2,2^3\Rightarrow \quad 4 \sin ^2 \theta=1,3 \Rightarrow \sin ^2 \theta=\frac{1}{4},\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2\Rightarrow \quad \sin \theta=\frac{1}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{\pi}{3}$
Let the altitude of the sun be $\theta$. Then, \begin{aligned} & & \tan \theta & =\frac{h}{h / \sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow \tan \theta=\sqrt{3} \\ \Rightarrow \quad & & \theta & =\pi / 3 \Rightarrow \theta=2 \alpha \end{aligned}

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A house subtends a right angle at the window of a opposite house and the angle of elevation of the window from the bottom of the first house is $60$. If the distance between two houses be $6 \mathrm{~m}$, then the height of the first house is
questions.solution:
Let $P Q$ be the house subtending a right angle at the window $B$ of opposite house $A B$
In $\triangle P A B$, we have $\tan 60^{\circ}=\frac{A B}{6}=A B=6 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~m}$ In $\triangle C B Q$, we have $\tan 30^{\circ}=\frac{h-C P}{B C}\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{h-6 \sqrt{3}}{6} \quad[\because A B=C P, B C=A P] \\ \Rightarrow & h=6\left(\sqrt{3}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) \\ \Rightarrow & h=8 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~m}\end{array}$

questions.q: $\mathrm{ABC}$ is a triangular park with $\mathrm{AB}=\mathrm{AC}=100 \mathrm{~m} . \mathrm{A}$ TV tower stands at the mid-point of $\mathrm{BC}$. The angles of elevation of the top of the tower at A, B, C are $45^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}$ respectively. The height of the tower is
questions.solution:
$\tan 45^{\circ}=\frac{\mathrm{PQ}}{\mathrm{AQ}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{AQ}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{h}=\mathrm{AQ}$ Where $\mathrm{PQ}$ is tower and $\mathrm{ABC}$ is the park, with $\mathrm{Q}$ being mid point of the side $\mathrm{BC}$ and $\mathrm{PQ}=\mathrm{h}$ Also, $A Q^{2}+B Q^{2}=100^{2}\Rightarrow \mathrm{h}^{2}+\mathrm{h}^{2} \cot ^{2} 60^{\circ}=100^{2}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{h}^{2}\left[1+\frac{1}{3}\right]=100^{2}\Rightarrow \mathrm{h}^{2}=\frac{3 \times 100^{2}}{4} \Rightarrow \mathrm{h}=50 \sqrt{3}$
